item.title: Technical Debt And Project Management
item.description:
Introduction Link to heading

I’ve been working on an experimental project and as I was working through it, I started saying things like, “I need to come back to this later” or adding TODOs all over the place, even though I’m not planning on taking the project further it really got me thinking about technical debt in software why it’s not addressed sooner.

I’ve Seen This Movie Link to heading

I’ve been working as a software developer for 10+ years and have joined projects that are in various stages. One thing that always pops up is developers mentioning that they need some time to clean things up but that there is never time to actually do so.

item.title: Testing A Reusable Django App
item.description:
Introduction Link to heading

I recently created a reuseable django app and was wondering how I’d go about testing it without creating an entire django application. Lucky for us, django has got an example for how to go about it.

The example was not enough for me as my application consisted of a couple of REST apis and using the above example required me to add a few more things, so lets go through the steps that were required.

item.title: Adding Extra Info on Plotly Charts on Hover
item.description:
Plotly is my goto library when it’s time to create visualizations. Its a very easy to use high level library with an array of customization’s.

Creating a chart is as simple as

var data = [
	{
	    x: [1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9],
	    y: [1,2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16,18],
	    type:'bar'
	}
    ];
    Plotly.newPlot('myDiv',data);

where myDiv is the id of the HTML element you want the chart to be inserted in.

Giving us a very nice looking bar chart.

item.title: Concept - Django project as a debian package
item.description:
Concept - Django project as a debian package Link to heading

For the past couple of months I’ve been pondering whether it would be possible to package a full django project as debian package (.deb).

Now and then I tend to write small web applications that run on my machine and use the SQLite database. On one occasion somebody asked if they could run the application on their machine.
